The binary totient series

Open Problem on GitHub
ResultsPapersLean mapWhat is checked

Results and open questions

#249. The short paper proves the all-base finite-level rank 𝑘𝑒 +1ke+1 for every 𝑘 ≥2k≥2 and 𝑒 ≥1e≥1, with canonical integral coordinates and a basis of all integral relations; at prime base the rank is exponential in the depth 𝑒e. A rational 5/45/4 control that agrees with totient on odd arguments still has tempered carry rank at least 2𝑒 −12e−1 at every depth, so a generic rationality-driven carry-rank ceiling is false. Bounded-residue series 𝐴𝑚Am remain irrational for every 𝑚 ≥3m≥3, with a complete rationality classification at dyadic moduli; this is ordinary mathematics in the short note, not Lean. The strongest checked structural result on the hypothetical rational totient branch is carry anti-compression: one carry would have uniformly eventually-periodic dyadic sections modulo its multiplier while retaining canonical section rank at least 2𝑒 −12e−1 at every level. No finite-rank upper bound is proved, so this is a necessary consequence rather than a contradiction. Finite denominator exclusions and conditional actual-LCM and first-harmonic routes remain useful, but none supplies the missing cofinal producer. Coons non-regularity, Martin affine independence, and Yazdani–Shallit CRT–Dirichlet separation are credited antecedents, not new claims of this release.

A basis and all its relations

We write 𝜑φ for Euler’s totient function and use ℕ ={0,1,2,…}N={0,1,2,…}, with 𝜑(0) =0φ(0)=0. For 𝑘 ≥2k≥2, the 𝑘k-kernel consists of the sequences 𝑛 ↦𝜑(𝑘𝑗𝑛 +𝑟)n↦φ(kjn+r) with 𝑗 ≥0j≥0 and 0 ≤𝑟 <𝑘𝑗0≤r<kj. Some of these sections are scalar multiples of others: for example, 𝜑(4𝑛 +2) =𝜑(2𝑛 +1)φ(4n+2)=φ(2n+1) and 𝜑(4𝑛) =2𝜑(2𝑛)φ(4n)=2φ(2n). Thus the seven sections through level two in base two are spanned by

𝑛⟼𝜑(𝑛),𝜑(2𝑛),𝜑(2𝑛+1),𝜑(4𝑛+1),𝜑(4𝑛+3).n⟼φ(n),φ(2n),φ(2n+1),φ(4n+1),φ(4n+3).

Are these five sequences independent, and do the analogous reductions account for every relation in every base? The next theorem answers both questions; Corollary 1.3 gives the integral relation module.

An integer sequence is 𝑘k-regular if the ℤZ-module generated by its 𝑘k-kernel is finitely generated [1]. Coons proved that the totient sequence is not 𝑘k-regular for any 𝑘 ≥2k≥2 [2]. Martin’s Theorem 1 already implies the affine independence used below [4]. The theorem below identifies the finite-level basis and all integral relations.

The assertion concerns the integer combinations of the original sections, not every integer-valued sequence in their rational span. For example, at base 22 and 𝑒 ≥2e≥2, 𝜑(4𝑛 +3)/2φ(4n+3)/2 takes integer values but has coefficient 1/21/2 in the retained basis. The generated module is therefore not saturated in the group of integer-valued sequences: an integer-valued sequence outside the module can have a nonzero integer multiple inside it.

Relations with periodic coefficients

Pairwise nonproportionality is essential here. For instance, 𝑛 +1n+1 and 𝑛 +2n+2 satisfy the hypothesis. In contrast, 4𝑛 +24n+2 and 2𝑛 +12n+1 are proportional, and 𝜑(4𝑛 +2) =𝜑(2𝑛 +1)φ(4n+2)=φ(2n+1) gives a nontrivial relation. Periodicity imposes no bound on the common period: it permits any finite periodic pattern, because one can work on each residue class separately.

Corollary 1.4 (Periodic coefficients). Let 𝐿1,…,𝐿𝑠L1,…,Ls be pairwise nonproportional affine forms with integer coefficients and positive slopes. If 𝑤1,…,𝑤𝑠w1,…,ws are rational-valued periodic sequences, then

∑𝑖𝑤𝑖(𝑛)𝜑(𝐿𝑖(𝑛))=0for all sufficiently large 𝑛⟹𝑤𝑖(𝑛)=0for every 𝑖,𝑛.∑iwi(n)φ(Li(n))=0for all sufficiently large n⟹wi(n)=0for every i,n.

Lean: periodic freezing integer affine.

Proof. Write 𝐿𝑖(𝑛) =𝑎𝑖𝑛 +𝑏𝑖Li(n)=ain+bi and choose a common positive period 𝑄Q for the 𝑤𝑖wi. On a progression 𝑛 =𝑟 +𝑄𝑡n=r+Qt, with 0 ≤𝑟 <𝑄0≤r<Q, their values are the constants 𝑤𝑖(𝑟)wi(r). The restricted affine forms have cross determinants 𝑄(𝑎𝑖𝑏𝑗 −𝑎𝑗𝑏𝑖) ≠0Q(aibj−ajbi)≠0. Shifting 𝑡t beyond the stated threshold preserves these determinants and makes all arguments positive. Affine independence then gives 𝑤𝑖(𝑟) =0wi(r)=0 for every 𝑖i. Doing this for each residue 𝑟r proves the conclusion at all indices, by periodicity. ◻

Applied on each progression, Martin’s Theorem 1 gives the same conclusion [4]. The same argument preserves the basis after deletion of a finite prefix. For the two sections with residue zero, large 𝑛 ≡1(mod𝑘)n≡1(modk) and large powers of 𝑘k replace the two evaluations used above.

Scope.

This completes the basis argument. It describes relations among coefficient subsequences, not the arithmetic nature of 𝑆 =∑𝑛≥1𝜑(𝑛)2−𝑛S=∑n≥1φ(n)2−n.

Supplementary results on the binary totient series

The independent results below distinguish bounded-residue series, finite exclusions for 𝑆S, and conditions for irrationality. None is needed for Theorem 1.1; in particular, the conditions in Sections 3 and 5 are not assumptions of that theorem. Generating-function context and the formal-source guide are in Appendix A.

Bounded residues and rationality

After reducing 𝜑(𝑛)φ(n) modulo a fixed integer, the coefficients are bounded. A single nonzero coefficient between long zero blocks then contradicts rationality by an elementary tail estimate.

Theorem 2.1 (Residue series and dyadic observables). For every 𝑚 ≥3m≥3,

∑𝑛≥1𝜑(𝑛)mod𝑚2𝑛∉ℚ.∑n≥1φ(n)modm2n∉Q.

For 𝑘 ≥1k≥1 and 𝑓 :ℤ/2𝑘ℤ →ℚf:Z/2kZ→Q, the series ∑𝑛≥1𝑓(𝜑(𝑛)mod2𝑘)2−𝑛∑n≥1f(φ(n)mod2k)2−n is rational exactly when 𝑓f is constant on the even residue classes. If that constant is 𝑐c, its value is 3𝑓(1)/4 +𝑐/43f(1)/4+c/4.

Lean: short note residue theorem.

The restriction 𝑚 ≥3m≥3 is necessary: modulo 22 the only nonzero coefficients occur at 𝑛 =1,2n=1,2, and the sum is 1/2 +1/4 =3/41/2+1/4=3/4. For the second assertion, only 𝑓(1)f(1) and its values on the even classes can affect the sum. The other odd classes are never attained by 𝜑(𝑛)φ(n).

The next lemma applies, for example, to the indicator of the squares: its coefficients are bounded, and sufficiently large squares have no other square within any prescribed distance. An eventually periodic sequence with infinitely many nonzero terms cannot satisfy the isolated-coefficient hypothesis. Most importantly, the bound 𝐶C must be fixed before the zero blocks are chosen; the unbounded coefficients 𝜑(𝑛)φ(n) do not satisfy this hypothesis.

The long record gives the same decomposition, and the four simultaneous inequalities are defined in the linked source. All four bounds must hold on the same block with the same parameters. The permitted blocks need only be arbitrarily large, but 𝐿L must also make the truncation error small enough for the residue test. The long record proves the unassigned and excluded-cofactor bounds at minimal admissible depth, using smooth-number asymptotics and the distribution of 𝜑(𝑚)/𝑚φ(m)/m. The unassigned bound is also a Lean theorem, whose proof replaces the smooth-number asymptotics by Mertens’ theorems. An elementary mean-value estimate also gives the explicit sufficient cutoff 𝜂 =1/1000η=1/1000 for the excluded-cofactor bound. The two remaining estimates concern the group means and their weighted, mean-subtracted phases. Further context and formal sources

Affine independence in the earlier literature

The separation method has an earlier source: Yazdani’s proof of Theorem 2, explicitly credited there to Shallit, uses the Chinese remainder theorem and Dirichlet’s theorem to distinguish kernel sections modulo a fixed modulus [10]. For a later account see Allouche, Shallit and Yassawi [11]. Here one separates a chosen column from every other column of a finite evaluation matrix. Nonsingularity, not merely distinctness of infinitely many sections, gives linear independence.

Martin’s Theorem 1 gives another proof of the affine independence conclusion [4]. For any ordering of the nonproportional forms and any 𝐶 >0C>0, their successive totient ratios exceed 𝐶C on a set of positive lower density. In a proposed relation ∑𝑖𝑐𝑖𝜑(𝐿𝑖(𝑛)) =0∑iciφ(Li(n))=0, put a nonzero coefficient first and choose 𝐶 >max(1,∑𝑖>1|𝑐𝑖|/|𝑐1|)C>max(1,∑i>1|ci|/|c1|). At the resulting values of 𝑛n, the first term has larger absolute value than the sum of all the others, a contradiction. The proof in Section 1.1 instead constructs a finite nonsingularity certificate for each chosen family.

Regularity, Mahler equations and section maps

The totient is not 𝑘k-regular, in the sense of Allouche and Shallit [1], for any 𝑘 ≥2k≥2: Coons proved that the ℤZ-module generated by its 𝑘k-kernel is not finitely generated, by counting the poles of 𝜁(𝑠 −1)/𝜁(𝑠)ζ(s−1)/ζ(s) in the strip 0 ≤Re⁡𝑠 ≤10≤Re⁡s≤1 . For integer-valued sequences this is equivalent to infinite dimension of the rational span: if the span has dimension 𝑑d, some 𝑑d evaluations map it injectively to ℚ𝑑Qd and the module into ℤ𝑑Zd (compare the evaluation argument in [3]). Theorem 1.1 therefore recovers Coons’s nonregularity theorem [2] and gives the dimension at every finite level.

The generating-function conclusion concerns functional equations, not just the dimensions of section spans. A 𝑘k-Mahler equation for a formal power series 𝐹F has the form

𝑑∑𝑖=0𝑃𝑖(𝑧)𝐹(𝑧𝑘𝑖)=0,𝑑≥0,𝑃𝑖(𝑧)∈ℚ[𝑧],𝑃0≠0.∑i=0dPi(z)F(zki)=0,d≥0,Pi(z)∈Q[z],P0≠0.

The height criterion of Adamczewski, Bell and Smertnig already implies that an integer-coefficient 𝑘k-Mahler series with polynomially bounded coefficients is 𝑘k-regular [14]. Indeed, the logarithmic height of an integer 𝑎a is log⁡max(1,|𝑎|)log⁡max(1,|a|). Since 0 ≤𝜑(𝑛) ≤𝑛0≤φ(n)≤n, nonregularity rules out such an equation for 𝐹𝜑(𝑧) =∑𝑛≥1𝜑(𝑛)𝑧𝑛Fφ(z)=∑n≥1φ(n)zn in every base 𝑘 ≥2k≥2; no multiplicativity hypothesis is needed for this deduction. The multiplicative classification in Bell and Smertnig’s later preprint also gives this conclusion [12]. Bell, Bruin and Coons give related classifications for algebraic or 𝐷D-finite generating functions ; 𝐷D-finite means satisfying a linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. These theorems constrain the whole generating function. They do not by themselves determine the arithmetic nature of its single value 𝐹𝜑(1/2)Fφ(1/2).

For example, the next dyadic level has rank 99 rather than 1515: 𝜑(8𝑛 +2) =𝜑(4𝑛 +1)φ(8n+2)=φ(4n+1), 𝜑(8𝑛 +4) =2𝜑(2𝑛 +1)φ(8n+4)=2φ(2n+1) and 𝜑(8𝑛 +6) =𝜑(4𝑛 +3)φ(8n+6)=φ(4n+3) are its positive-residue reductions.

For a 𝑘k-regular sequence that is not eventually zero, its growth exponent is the base-𝑘k logarithm of the joint spectral radius of the section matrices in a basis of the kernel span. A redundant spanning family gives only an upper bound [3]. This finite-dimensional theorem does not apply to 𝜑φ. Its section maps nevertheless have the explicit form below. For 0 ≤𝑖 <𝑘0≤i<k, put 𝑇𝑖𝑔(𝑛) =𝑔(𝑘𝑛 +𝑖)Tig(n)=g(kn+i). These are the coefficient versions of the Cartier operators, and

𝑇𝑖𝐹𝑗,𝑟=𝐹𝑗+1,𝑘𝑗𝑖+𝑟,𝑉𝑘,𝑒+1=𝑉𝑘,𝑒+𝑘−1∑𝑖=0𝑇𝑖𝑉𝑘,𝑒.TiFj,r=Fj+1,kji+r,Vk,e+1=Vk,e+∑i=0k−1TiVk,e.

Write each residue at level 𝑗 +1j+1 as 𝑘𝑗𝑖 +𝑟kji+r, 0 ≤𝑟 <𝑘𝑗0≤r<kj, to obtain the second equality. The strict dimension increase therefore prevents all 𝑇𝑖Ti from preserving 𝑉𝑘,𝑒Vk,e. A retained positive-residue section maps to another such section, since 𝑘 ∤(𝑘𝑗𝑖 +𝑟)k∤(kji+r) when 𝑗 ≥1j≥1 and 𝑘 ∤𝑟k∤r. The two zero-residue generators need separate treatment: 𝑇𝑖𝐹0,0 =𝐹1,𝑖TiF0,0=F1,i and 𝑇𝑖𝐹1,0 =𝐹2,𝑘𝑖TiF1,0=F2,ki, the latter a positive integer multiple of 𝐹1,𝑖F1,i. Thus every basis element maps to a positive integer multiple of a basis element at the next level, not necessarily to a basis element itself.

Erdős and Graham list the irrationality question for 𝑆S [8].

Formal verification and finite certificates

Formal support.

The dyadic infinite-basis corollary and the periodic-coefficient corollary have ordinary proofs above; no additional formal declarations are asserted for them. For Lemma 2.2, the supplied release records acceptance by the Lean kernel and by NanoDa at Palomar’s Comparator stage. No new replay was performed for this revision.

Formal sources: wcook04/plectis-erdos-lean; run 34782407633.

  1. Rank in every integer base. Theorem 1.1 proves that the sections through level 𝑒 ≥1e≥1 have rank 𝑘𝑒 +1ke+1 for every 𝑘 ≥2k≥2. The formal proof separates the dimension count from the independence argument. An older theorem assumes independence; the linked Chinese-remainder and Dirichlet argument proves that assumption. The resulting rank theorem is unconditional and does not use Martin’s theorem as an axiom. The sources are exact finite-truncation rank; the same count from an independent family; the independence argument in every base; complete truncation rank.

The long record also gives the exact Farey-interval certificate at window 𝐾 =240K=240, excluding 𝑆 =𝑎/𝑞S=a/q for integers 𝑎a and 0 <𝑞 ≤𝑄0 ≈7.96 ×10340<q≤Q0≈7.96×1034. This finite exclusion is separate from the quantified irrationality conditions.

Formal sources: dyadic finite-level rank 2𝑒 +12e+1; propagation with depth equal to the shift; lower bound for the rank-one quotients; the unconditional all-base rank theorem; Rank from an independent all-base family; the equivalent residue condition.

What is checked in Lean
  • For every 𝑒 ≥1e≥1, the complete dyadic totient kernel through level e has rational span dimension 2𝑒 +12e+1.
  • The rational span of the full dyadic totient kernel is not finite-dimensional; for integer-valued sequence modules this is equivalent to Coons's non-k-regularity and is not an independent contribution.
  • Lean diagonal certificates through 𝑡 =82t=82; neither 𝑡 =83t=83 nor an unbounded family is supplied.
  • Conditionally: a cofinal strict 9/109/10 gap for the exact natural prime-tail orbit supplies the existing finite pivot-point escape and hence the reviewed irrationality endpoint.
  • The local s=1 and s=2 squared Möbius Euler-factor identities and the first two prime-power divisor-sum differences.
  • That the two-by-two checkerboard kills separable backgrounds and is unique up to scale under the four row and column cancellations.
  • An abstract four-point divisor-layer identity, stated from its four explicit factorisation hypotheses.
  • An affine completion no-go: every residue class modulo an even modulus has a digit that recentres one carry step.
  • Exact producer and consumer interfaces for prime-ray layer supply, bounded-degree order witnesses, and finite-prime-support escape.
What is not checked
  • The strict prime-tail orbit gap, which is the unproved producer consumed by the conditional endpoint.
  • The packet's sharp parabolic Stern-Brocot cusp theorem and its passage from a geometric x-parameter to the arithmetic totient series.
  • Eventual Hankel nonvanishing for the Möbius-Mersenne power ladder, or its denominator obstruction.
  • The natural-boundary and quasimodular-transcendence steps of the infinite Euler-sieve tower.
  • Polynomial resultant realisability, exact-order finite-field supply, Frobenius freezing, or the Archimedean growth needed by the prime-ray strategy.
  • Unconditional irrationality of the binary totient series.
The formal record: 15 main results, 5 open obligations, 3 Lean modules, finite search evidence, Comparator review

Main results

Statements and boundaries are copied from the corpus record. Registry status: registered_declarations

locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: totient_kernel_rank

For every 𝑒 ≥1e≥1, the complete dyadic totient kernel through level e has rational span dimension 2𝑒 +12e+1.

This does not prove irrationality of the totient series.

Erdos249257.finrank_totientKernelThroughLevelFamily_eq
Lean formalisation of an existing consequence of Coons family: totient_kernel_rank

The rational span of the full dyadic totient kernel is not finite-dimensional.

The declaration is kernel-checked locally, but full-kernel infinite-dimensionality is not an independent contribution of this release; no rationality-to-finite-rank bridge is proved.

Erdos249257.not_finiteDimensional_span_fullTotientKernel
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: totient_kernel_basis

The full dyadic totient kernel span admits the explicit odd-core-indexed basis.

The basis theorem does not connect rationality to finite kernel rank.

Erdos249257.totientDyadicSectionBasis
formalised unconditional spanning and conditional rank with external independence input family: totient_kernel_all_base_index

Under 2 ≤𝑘,1 ≤𝑒2≤k,1≤e, and linear independence of the explicit canonical all-base family, the actual all-base totient kernel through level e has rational span dimension 𝑘𝑒 +1ke+1.

The linear-independence hypothesis is the external affine-ordering boundary and is not proved here; this does not prove irrationality of the binary totient series.

Erdos249257.finrank_allBaseTotientKernelThroughLevelFamily_eq_of_linearIndependent
formalised exact visible-lattice normalization identity family: totient_visible_coprime_lattice_mass

The positive coprime Mersenne weights over the visible lattice sum exactly to one, giving the reduced-direction mass behind the fair-coin coprimality form of the totient constant.

This is a rational normalization identity and does not prove irrationality of the binary totient series or settle Erdős #249.

GcdMomentCalculus.tsum_pos_coprime_inv_mersenne_eq_one
formalised exact first-gcd-moment squared-Lambert transfer identity family: squared_lambert_gcd_moments

At base one half, the squared-Mersenne Lambert series weighted by Euler's totient equals the dyadic series of Pillai's gcd-sum function minus n, the exact first gcd-moment transfer.

This exact identity does not prove irrationality of the binary totient series; the constant-weight squared-Lambert irrationality is cited external mathematics, and no Erdős #249 endpoint follows.

GcdMomentCalculus.tsum_totient_div_mersenne_sq_eq_gcd_moment_series
formalised exact Fibonacci/continuant run stability floor family: stern_brocot_run_fibonacci_stability

For every finite defect list e, the height of the corresponding positive Stern-Brocot run word is at least 𝐹𝑟+3 +𝐹𝑟+1Fr+3+Fr+1 times the total defect, where r is the number of runs.

This exact combinatorial stability floor does not establish analytic denominator survival, irrationality of the binary totient series, or novelty; no Erdős #249 endpoint follows.

SternBrocotRunGeometry.runHeight_defect_fib_sum_lower
formalised exact Stern-Brocot cylinder telescoping identity family: stern_brocot_cylinder_law

At every positive Stern-Brocot node (a,b), the closed cylinder mass splits exactly into the node's stop mass and the two child cylinder masses.

This exact telescoping recursion and its geometric interpretation do not prove irrationality of the binary totient series or novelty; the #249 endpoint remains open.

GcdMomentCalculus.cylinderMass_split
unconditional progress family: lcm_factor_ideal_shift_algebra_no_go

For every 𝑡 ≥3t≥3, a nonzero synthetic dyadic coboundary survives every finite integer shift polynomial while retaining the period-LCM totient factor ideals, exact cleared-prefix cancellation, and uniform state and letter bounds.

The witness is synthetic: it does not assert that its forcing letters are actual totient differences, does not address nonlinear combinations, and leaves the unbounded certificate supply for Erdős #249 open.

Erdos249257.TotientTailPeriodKiller.lcm_factorIdeal_finiteRank_shiftAlgebra_not_sufficient
unconditional synthetic no-go; novelty unassessed family: fixed_precision_transport_no_go

For every positive fixed precision, every finite word of odd valuation-unit symbols and every incoming integer carry state admit a compatible orbit whose successive states stay within the corresponding valuation-unit radii; fixed-precision local signatures therefore do not by themselves exclude finite centred completions.

This is a synthetic finite-word construction with unrestricted incoming/high quotient states. It does not impose the actual totient-difference relation or provide growing-precision/global correlation, and it gives no Erdős #249 endpoint or irrationality result. No novelty or priority claim is made. The one-step and finite-word completion theorems are subordinate mechanisms, not separate families.

Erdos249257.TotientTailPeriodKiller.fixedPrecisionTropicalNoGo
conditional reduction family: actual_lcm_orbit_separation

A cofinal quantitative separation supply for the actual power-two LCM tail orbit implies irrationality of the binary totient series.

The cofinal separation supply is an open premise, stronger than mere non-integrality; this sufficient route is not an equivalence and leaves the punctured/top-edge boundary and the Erdős #249 endpoint open.

Erdos249257.DiagonalFreshLossBridge.PowerTwoOddWindowAffine.irrational_totientSeries_of_actualLcmOrbitSeparationSupply
conditional reduction family: actual_foreign_residue_projection

The finite Möbius residue diagonal splits into projected foreign and divisor channels, every finite stable foreign-tail window obeys a closed geometric bound, and a controlled projection separated from every integer forces the full target to be missed.

This is a conditional finite partition/geometric-majorant reduction with a generic complement-noncancellation consumer. The ControlledForeignProjection analytic bridge and any unbounded separated-projection supply remain unproved; no Erdős #249 endpoint, novelty, significance, priority, or external-review claim is made.

conditional reduction family: first_harmonic_pivot_decomposition

ErdosProblems.Erdos249.irrational_totient_series_of_naturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap
locally proved necessary consequence; novelty unassessed family: totient_carry_anti_compression

If the binary totient coefficient series were rational, one positive-multiplier tempered integral carry has dyadic sections uniformly eventually periodic modulo its multiplier and canonical carry-section span dimension at least 2𝑒2e − 1 for every e.

This is a necessary consequence of rationality only: it gives no contradiction, no finite-rank upper bound for a rationality-supplied carry, and no irrationality proof for Erdős #249. Modulo a divisor of the multiplier, the forcing disappears and the carry becomes geometric, so quotient periodicity alone supplies no finite-ℚ-rank upper bound. The coefficient-side kernel-rank and certificate-equivalence families are not duplicated, and #249 remains open.
